title: Recorded Deposit Grade and the Damages Share of C&I Termination Security
content:
For Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts, the termination security's damages portion is scaled by the grade recorded on the contract's posted security deposit, which is the commercial credit grade used when the contract was executed and not the grade on the customer profile today: a deposit recording grade A scales the damages by 0.50, a deposit recording grade B scales them by 0.75, and a deposit recording grade C or not rated, or no posted deposit, leaves them in full.

The grade is the credit grade basis shown on the contract's security deposit receipt; where the contract carries more than one receipt, the most recently posted receipt is read. Scaling multiplies the damages portion by the share shown.

| Grade recorded on the contract's posted security deposit | Damages portion multiplied by |
|---|---|
| A | 0.50 (50%) |
| B | 0.75 (75%) |
| C | 1, in full |
| not rated | 1, in full |
| no posted deposit on the contract | 1, in full |

## Points of judgement

- The customer profile shows grade A today, but the contract's deposit receipt records grade C: the damages are taken in full, because the recorded grade governs.
- The profile shows grade C today, but the receipt records grade B: the damages are scaled by 0.75.
- A contract with no security deposit receipt at all: the damages are taken in full.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A damages portion of $12000.00 becomes 12000.00 multiplied by 0.50, that is $6000.00, under a receipt recording grade A; $9000.00 under grade B; and stays $12000.00 under grade C, not rated or no receipt.
